Drone Flight Log

User Manual for iPhone

Offline progressive web app (PWA) for logging sUAS flight hours by drone type and date. Install from Safari · data stays on your phone.

1. Install on iPhone

The app is a website that can sit on your Home Screen like a normal app. Use Safari (not Chrome or other browsers) so “Add to Home Screen” works.

  1. Open Safari and go to:
    https://rons2438.github.io/flightlog/
  2. Tap the Share button (square with an arrow pointing up).
  3. Scroll the share sheet and tap Add to Home Screen.
  4. Confirm the name Flight Log (or edit it) and tap Add.
  5. Open the new Home Screen icon. The app runs full-screen without the Safari address bar.
Tip: After an update is published to GitHub Pages, fully close the Home Screen app (swipe it away from the app switcher) and open it again so the new version loads.

2. Quick start

  1. Tap Add at the bottom.
  2. Pick the Date and Drone type.
  3. Enter duration as Hours + min, or switch to Start / end times.
  4. Optionally fill serial, location, mission, role, day/night, and notes.
  5. Tap Save flight.
  6. See it on the Log tab. Check totals on Totals.
  7. When you have a few flights, open Settings → Back up to iCloud and save the file to Files → iCloud Drive.

4. Adding, editing, and deleting flights

Add a flight

  1. Tap Add.
  2. Date — defaults to today; change if needed.
  3. Drone type — choose from the list. Built-in starters are RQ-11 Raven, RQ-20 Puma, Skydio X2, DJI Mavic, and Other. Tap + New type to add another name for this flight.
  4. Duration entry
    • Hours + min — enter hours and minutes separately.
    • Start / end — enter start and end times. Overnight flights (end after midnight) are counted correctly.
  5. Optional fields: Aircraft / serial / tail #, Location, Mission / purpose, Pilot role (PIC, VO, Instructor, Student), Day / Night / Mixed, Notes.
  6. Tap Save flight.
If you turn on Ask to save to iCloud after each new flight in Settings, a banner appears after save with Save to iCloud and Not now.

Edit a flight

  1. On the Log tab, tap a flight row.
  2. The Add form opens filled in. The main button becomes Update flight, and Delete / Cancel appear.
  3. Change any fields, then tap Update flight, or Cancel to leave without saving.
Figure 5. Editing a flight — Update flight, Delete, and Cancel

Delete a flight

  1. Open the flight from the Log.
  2. Tap Delete, then confirm.

Search and filter (Log tab)

  • Search box — matches notes, location, serial, mission, role, day/night, and type text.
  • Type — All types or one type.
  • From / To — date range.

5. Totals

The Totals tab summarizes every flight on the phone:

  • Stat cards: Total hours, Flights, This month, Last 30 days, Last 90 days, This year.
  • Hours by type — bar list per drone type.
  • Hours by month — chart for the last 12 months plus month bars.
  • Email Export — share a CSV (see next section).
  • Download CSV — save the CSV file directly.
If Log filters (type, dates, or search) are set, Email Export and CSV export use the filtered list. Clear filters to export everything.

6. Exporting by email

You can start an email export from Totals or from Settings → Other export / import.

  1. Tap Email Export.
  2. iPhone opens the share sheet with a CSV file attached (FlightLog_YYYY-MM-DD.csv). Tap Mail (or another app).
  3. If sharing files is not available, the app falls back: it may share a text summary and/or download the CSV, or open a mailto: draft with the summary so you can attach the downloaded CSV yourself.

CSV columns: Date, Type, Hours_HMM, Hours_Decimal, Minutes, Serial, Location, Mission, Role, DayNight, Start, End, Notes, Id.

You can also tap CSV or Download CSV / JSON backup in Settings to download files without emailing.

7. Importing a spreadsheet

Excel (.xlsx) is not supported in the browser. Save as CSV first, then import.

Save Excel or Numbers as CSV

  1. Open the workbook in Excel or Numbers.
  2. Choose File → Save As (or Export) → CSV (UTF-8 if offered).
  3. Put the .csv file somewhere you can reach from the phone (Files, iCloud Drive, email, AirDrop).

Import into the app

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Under Other export / import, choose Merge or Replace (this toggle applies to Import JSON and Import CSV).
    • Merge — adds new rows; duplicates are skipped.
    • Replace — overwrites current flights/types (you will be asked to confirm for JSON replace).
  3. Tap Import CSV and pick your file.
  4. In Map CSV columns, match your spreadsheet headers to: Date *, Type / aircraft / platform *, Duration *, and optional Serial, Location, Mission, Role, Day/Night, Notes, Start time, End time. The app guesses common header names.
  5. Review the preview stats/table, then tap Import.

Date formats the importer accepts

  • YYYY-MM-DD (example: 2026-11-05)
  • M/D/YYYY, M-D-YYYY, or M.D.YYYY (2-digit years supported)
  • D-Mon-YY, D-Mon-YYYY, or D Mon YY (example: 5-Nov-26)
  • Mon D, YYYY (example: Nov 5, 2026)

Duration values

  • H:MM or HH:MM:SS
  • Decimal hours (default for plain numbers)
  • Minutes when the column header suggests minutes, or when the number looks like minutes
Duplicates: rows with the same date + type + duration + notes as an existing flight (or another row in the same import) are skipped. New drone type names in the CSV are added automatically.

You can also use Import JSON for a full droneFlightLog.v1 backup file (see Backup).

8. Backing up and restoring

Flights live in the phone’s browser storage (localStorage). Automatic snapshots also save to IndexedDB on the same phone. Neither survives losing the phone or clearing Safari website data — use iCloud (or Mail / AirDrop) for that.

Figure 6. Settings → Backup & restore

Back up to iCloud

  1. On Log (when you have flights) or Settings, tap Back up to iCloud.
  2. The share sheet opens with a file named like flightlog-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.json.
  3. Tap Save to Files, then choose iCloud Drive (or Mail / AirDrop).
  4. A Backup ready screen appears with a tappable link to the backup file, its date, and flight count. Tap Done.
Figure 7. Backup ready
Figure 8. Restore preview — Merge or Replace
A web app cannot write to iCloud by itself. Saving always needs that one tap on Save to Files. The app also cannot open a deep link into the file’s folder inside iCloud Drive — use the Files app → iCloud Drive.

Latest backup file links

In Settings you will see:

  • Latest backup file — a download link (filename, date, flight count). After you share to iCloud, this reflects that backup; before the first share it can show the current log as a downloadable file.
  • Latest automatic on-phone snapshot — link to the newest local snapshot (stored only on this iPhone).
  • Last iCloud backup status line — shows when you last backed up; warns if never, older than 14 days, or if new flights were added since then.

Ask to save to iCloud after each new flight

In Settings, check Ask to save to iCloud after each new flight (off by default). After each new save, a banner offers Save to iCloud or Not now.

Automatic on-phone backups

  • A snapshot is written on this device every time you add, edit, delete, or import a flight.
  • The last about 10 snapshots are kept (IndexedDB).
  • Under Automatic on-phone backups, each snapshot lists when it was taken and how many flights it holds, with a per-snapshot Restore button.
  • These protect against accidental deletes on this phone. They do not protect against losing the phone or clearing Safari data alone (IndexedDB may also be cleared with website data).
If Safari clears the main log but an on-phone snapshot still exists, the app may offer Restore automatic backup? with Restore or Start fresh.

Restore from Backup

  1. Tap Restore from Backup (Settings, or the empty-log welcome button).
  2. Pick a flightlog-backup-….json from Files / iCloud Drive.
  3. Read the preview (flight count, date range, file date, drone types, how many flights are on this phone).
  4. Choose Merge (skips flights that already exist with the same id) or Replace (wipes this phone’s log first), or Cancel.

JSON backup / Import JSON under Other export / import use the same JSON format; Merge/Replace for those imports is controlled by the Merge | Replace segment above the hints.

9. Moving to a new iPhone

Flight data does not move with iCloud Photos or a normal app restore. Move it with a backup file.

On the old iPhone

  1. Open Flight Log → Settings (or Log).
  2. Tap Back up to iCloud.
  3. Share sheet → Save to Files → iCloud Drive.
  4. Confirm the Backup ready screen shows your flight count.

On the new iPhone

  1. In Safari open https://rons2438.github.io/flightlog/, then Share → Add to Home Screen.
  2. Open the app. With an empty log you will see:
    Moving from another iPhone? Restore from Backup
  3. Tap that button (or Settings → Restore from Backup).
  4. Choose the flightlog-backup-….json from Files → iCloud Drive.
  5. Preview the contents, then tap Replace (typical for a brand-new phone) or Merge.
  6. Check the Log and Totals tabs. Make a fresh Back up to iCloud from the new phone when you are happy.
Figure 9. Empty log — restore from another iPhone

10. Privacy

  • The app code is hosted publicly on GitHub Pages at the link above. Anyone can open the site.
  • Your flight data is not uploaded to GitHub. It stays in this phone’s Safari storage (localStorage) and optional on-phone IndexedDB snapshots.
  • Only you put a copy elsewhere — for example by Save to Files → iCloud Drive, Mail, AirDrop, or downloading CSV/JSON.
  • Clearing Safari website data for this site (or “Clear History and Website Data”) erases the log on that phone. Restore from an iCloud backup file if you have one.
  • Do not put a public GitHub repo’s contents behind a write token on the phone; that would risk exposing credentials. Prefer iCloud Drive for private backups.

11. Troubleshooting

Update not showing

  1. Fully close the Home Screen app (app switcher → swipe up).
  2. Open it again, or open the URL once in Safari to refresh the cache.
  3. If it still looks old, in Safari open the site, pull to refresh, then re-add to Home Screen if needed.

Share sheet not opening (Email Export or Back up to iCloud)

  • Use the Home Screen app or Safari on iPhone; desktop browsers often lack the same share-with-files behavior.
  • If share fails, the app downloads the file instead — use the Files save dialog or the Backup ready / Latest backup file link.
  • For email without an attachment, attach the downloaded FlightLog_….csv manually in Mail.

Import problems

  • Use CSV, not .xlsx.
  • In the map screen, ensure Date, Type, and Duration columns are mapped.
  • Check date formats listed in section 7.
  • If nothing imports, rows may all be duplicates of what you already have — try a small test CSV first.
  • For Replace on JSON, confirm the dialog; Merge never deletes existing flights by id collision rules described above.

Log is empty but you had flights

  • If offered, use Restore automatic backup?.
  • Otherwise Settings → Restore from Backup and pick your iCloud JSON file.

Add to Home Screen missing

You must use Safari. In Chrome on iPhone, Add to Home Screen is limited or absent for this install path.

12. FAQ

Does the app work offline?

Yes. After you have opened it once, a service worker caches the app shell so you can log flights without a network. Backups to iCloud still need you to use the share sheet when you choose.

Where is my data stored?

On the phone only (localStorage + optional IndexedDB snapshots), until you export or Back up to iCloud / share a file.

Can I sync automatically to GitHub?

Not recommended. The public Pages site would expose data, and a private repo would need a token on the phone. Use iCloud Drive instead.

What is the difference between JSON backup and CSV?

JSON (flightlog-backup-….json) is the full app backup (types + flights, same format as Import JSON / Restore). CSV is a spreadsheet-friendly export for email or Excel.

What does Merge vs Replace mean on Restore?

Merge keeps your current flights and adds ones from the file that are not already present (same id). Replace deletes the phone’s current log first, then loads the file.

How many automatic snapshots are kept?

About the last 10 on-phone snapshots.

Why does Last iCloud backup warn me?

If you have never backed up, the last backup is older than 14 days, or you have added flights since the last iCloud save, Settings highlights that status so you remember to share a new file.
